info.name: FacultyLens
info.description: FacultyLens API. 1) Run auth > POST /auth/login (it stores {{token}}). 2) Every other request sends Bearer {{token}}. Set baseUrl, username and password in the collection variables. Accounts created by the admin get a temporary password and must call change-password first.

request.description: Pings MongoDB. 200 ok, 503 degraded. Loads no model.
Which models are loaded, RAM, average latency. Loads nothing.
username = email (staff) or roll number (students). Sets the httpOnly refresh cookie (path /api/auth). Rate limited by LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT (default 5/minute per IP).
Uses the refresh cookie; rotates it and returns a new access token. 204 when there is no cookie (signed out); 401 when the token is expired, revoked or reused.
Required after the first sign-in with a temporary password (other routes return 403 password_change_required until then). New password: at least 10 characters.
Revokes the refresh token and clears the cookie.
Filters: role, department_id (admin only), q (name/email/roll number), include_inactive. A HoD always gets their own department.
Returns temp_password ONCE. Students need roll_no (ROLL_NO_REGEX); staff need email; gender is for faculty/HoD only and admin-only.
Validates every row: 422 bulk_invalid with per-row errors, or the number of valid rows. Without dry_run it creates all rows (all-or-nothing) and returns the credentials once.
CSV header: name,email,role,department_code,roll_no,gender (UTF-8, at most 1 MB and 1000 rows).
Soft delete: sets is_active=false and ends the user's sessions.
Admin: all; HoD: own department; faculty: the offerings they teach; student: their enrolments.
A course offering is unique per code + academic year + semester + section.
Student list only for admin and the department's HoD.
Add or remove students by roll number; faculty_ids (optional) replaces the teacher list. Unknown roll numbers are reported back.
Profile facts + pending imports + courses taught. Owner (faculty/HoD) and admin; a HoD can read their own department. can_edit tells the UI whether to show editing.
Replaces the editable sections. Items without an id get one; keep ids when editing so later grounding stays stable.

Fetches works, employments, educations and keywords from the public ORCID record (iD or orcid.org link, checksum verified) into pending_imports. Duplicates of accepted, pending or rejected items are skipped. Limited to 10/minute.
Candidate authors (id, affiliations, paper count, sample titles) so the faculty member can pick the right one.
Author ID or profile link. Papers go to pending_imports; a paper already pending from ORCID gets its citations and TL;DR filled in instead. TL;DRs are best-effort without S2_API_KEY.
Moves one pending item into its section; optional data overrides fields before saving.
Drops a pending item and remembers it so re-imports don't suggest it again.
Accept and reject many pending items in one call.
All cycles; admin also gets form, response and eligible counts.
Creates a draft. Odd term = semesters 1, 3, 5, 7.
What publishing would create, and offerings with no teacher.
Creates one teaching form per offering x teacher and one curriculum form per offering; opens the cycle. Idempotent.
Forms with response counts (never response content). HoD: own department only.
Open forms for the student's enrolled offerings, with submitted: true/false.
Questions, course, teacher. Students: only if enrolled. Staff: within their scope.

Teaching form shown; a curriculum form takes syllabus_relevance, outcomes_clarity, lab_adequacy, reference_material and texts.comment. One response per student per form: a second POST returns 409. Stores no student id, only a per-form HMAC code and the date.
Per teaching form: responses, eligible, min_required, and rating averages only once responses >= MIN_RESPONSES_FOR_DISPLAY. Comments stay hidden until Phase 4 moderates and redacts them.
Responses in the cycle, how many are analysed for the current model_version, and any active job.
Queues every unanalysed response in the cycle (202). Cached results are never re-scored; one active run per cycle.
done / total, counts of hidden, review, PII and sarcastic answers, timings.
Rebuilds every teaching-form summary in the cycle (202, a 'summaries' job). Summaries are otherwise rebuilt automatically when a form's aggregate changes.
A teacher's offerings in the cycle side by side (status, net score, rating, top strength and gap, sarcasm rate) plus all of them combined. The teacher, their HoD and admins.
Department overview: one row per teacher (never their gender), department aspects and totals. That department's HoD and admins. Without ?cycle the newest cycle with teaching forms is used.

Bias & sarcasm panel for one department, groups only: gendered-language rates per 1,000 answers, rating gap per aspect with a 95% Welch interval over teacher averages, emotion mix, sarcasm rate. status 'too_small' (sizes only) unless each group has BIAS_MIN_GROUP_FACULTY teachers and BIAS_MIN_GROUP_ANSWERS answers.
Possibly-sarcastic rate per teacher in the department (HoD, admin).
One teacher's possibly-sarcastic answer ids, for GET /faculty/:id/evidence.

Drafts the Action Taken rows (department x aspect and department x curriculum item; no teacher named) from stored aggregates. Re-drafting replaces only untouched drafts and keeps edited or approved rows.
All rows for the admin; a HoD gets their own department's rows.
Edit issue, action, responsible or timeline, and/or set status (draft | approved). An edit without status reopens an approved row. Admin, or the row's department HoD.
Adds a manual row (admin, or HoD for their department).

body.raw:
{
  "department_id": "{{departmentId}}",
  "label": "Library",
  "issue": "The library closes before evening classes end.",
  "action": "Keep the library open until 7 pm on weekdays.",
  "responsible": "Librarian"
}

request.description: Deletes a row (admin only). Drafted rows come back on the next re-draft if the data still supports them.
The redacted, visible student sentences behind a row (no teacher named).
Readiness for the final export: responses analysed, actions approved.
Watermarked 'DRAFT – not for submission' preview, available any time (admin). Without ?draft the export returns 409 until every row is approved.
The same report as Word, from the same content blocks as the PDF.
Creates a new draft from the accepted profile facts (Groq if configured, checked against the facts; otherwise a template). Owner or admin; 10/minute.
All drafts and approved versions, newest first. Owner, admin, and the department's HoD.
Edits a draft (409 once approved). Owner or admin.

body.raw:
{
  "headline": "Associate Professor, Computer Science and Engineering",
  "bio_short": "Teaches compilers and works on program analysis.",
  "bio_long": "Teaches compilers and works on program analysis and register allocation.",
  "research_areas": [
    "Compilers",
    "Program analysis"
  ],
  "key_achievements": [],
  "teaching_highlights": []
}

request.description: Only the faculty member can approve; the previous approved version becomes superseded.
The approved profile, readable by all staff (status 'none' until one is approved). Teaching highlights carry no evidence ids here.

The unified page in one call. Everyone on staff gets the profile; the owner, their HoD and admins also get cycles, offerings and the selected offering's insights, summary and sarcastic answer ids (status: available | awaiting_analysis | below_minimum).
Redacted, visible answers for up to 40 evidence ids, with the supporting sentence's offsets to highlight. Ids from other teachers, hidden answers or below-minimum forms are left out.
Answers the toxicity model hid (>= TOX_HIDE) or flagged for review (>= TOX_REVIEW), as redacted text with the flagged sentences.
approve (show it), hide (keep it from faculty), or redact with text (show an edited version). Audited; recomputes the form's aggregate.
Mark a staff account as 'annotator' (labels blind) or 'adjudicator' (settles disagreements); null clears it. Students can't be annotators.
The next comment this annotator hasn't labelled, without anyone else's label. Faculty/HoD annotators get only the public dataset; admin annotators also get the app's own redacted comments.
Save or replace my label. Skip with skip_reason (not_english | not_about_teaching | unclear) instead of a sentiment.
Counts per annotator, live Cohen's kappa once 30 comments have two labels, gold and open disagreements, and reference/grounding progress.
Up to 20 comments the two annotators labelled differently, with both labels.
The adjudicator's final label, which becomes the gold label.
One teacher's redacted comments (public dataset) to write a reference summary for.
1-4 strengths and 1-4 improvements; writing again replaces mine.
A generated summary's bullets with the evidence each cites, to mark as supported or not.
ml/results/evaluation.json as written by `python -m ml.evaluate`, or status not_run.
The usefulness survey: four 1-5 answers and a comment, one per teacher (answering again replaces it).
